record.paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
record.original_question: Find a Lyapunov-type theorem for Hamiltonian partial differential equations that is not of KAM type: under reasonable hypotheses, prove that most time-periodic solutions in any nondegenerate one-parameter family persist under small Hamiltonian perturbations of the equation.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3.1 (S. Kuksin) Find a Lyapounov Theorem (not of KAM type) for Hamiltonian PDEs. I.e. prove that (under reasonable assumptions) most of time-periodic solutions from any non-degenerate one-parameter family per­ sist under small Hamiltonian perturbations of the equation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a Hamiltonian partial differential equation written in the form
  u_t = J ∇H(u),
where u(t) belongs to a scale of Hilbert spaces, J is a (possibly unbounded) symplectic operator, and H is a smooth Hamiltonian functional. Assume that this equation possesses a nondegenerate one-parameter family

  {u_λ(t) : λ ∈ I ⊂ ℝ}

of time-periodic solutions with periods T(λ) depending on the parameter λ. Nondegeneracy is to be understood in a suitable Floquet/transversality sense (e.g. T'(λ) ≠ 0 and the linearized period map at u_λ has trivial kernel apart from the directions forced by symmetry).

Now perturb the Hamiltonian: replace H by H_ε = H + εK, where K is a smooth Hamiltonian functional and ε > 0 is small.

Problem. Establish a Lyapunov-type persistence theorem, not relying on Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser (KAM) techniques (i.e. avoiding Diophantine small-divisor iterations on Cantor-like sets of frequencies), under reasonable hypotheses on H, K, and the family {u_λ}, asserting that for sufficiently small |ε| a set of parameters λ ∈ I of large measure (in the sense that its complement has measure tending to zero as ε → 0) gives rise to time-periodic solutions of the perturbed equation u_t = J ∇H_ε(u) close to u_λ.

In other words: identify natural functional-analytic and nondegeneracy hypotheses on Hamiltonian PDEs under which the classical finite-dimensional Lyapunov center / persistence-of-periodic-orbits theorem extends, so that most periodic orbits in a nondegenerate one-parameter family survive small Hamiltonian perturbations, with a proof method that is not of KAM type.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search returns mainly Kuksin's KAM-type results for persistence of quasi-periodic and periodic solutions of Hamiltonian PDEs (e.g. his Handbook chapter and "Analysis of Hamiltonian PDEs"), but no clear non-KAM Lyapunov-type persistence theorem of the requested generality. The status of this problem could not be definitively verified from the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian PDEs (Handbook chapter), S. B. Kuksin
status_evidence.snippet: Kuksin's survey on Hamiltonian PDEs covers KAM-type persistence of periodic and quasi-periodic solutions; the problem of a non-KAM Lyapunov theorem is mentioned as an open direction.
status_evidence.claim: Existing persistence results for periodic solutions of Hamiltonian PDEs in this line are KAM-based, leaving the request for a non-KAM Lyapunov-type theorem open.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of Hamiltonian PDEs, S. B. Kuksin
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph developing KAM theory for Hamiltonian PDEs and persistence of finite-gap/periodic solutions.
status_evidence.claim: The standard reference treats persistence of periodic/quasi-periodic solutions via KAM, not via a Lyapunov-type approach.
